tagline: High-value export spice crop with premium returns
descriptionEn: High export cash spice crop commanding strong global demand. Protective sprays required during overcast humid weather.
imageAlt: Fragrant green cumin plants flowering with tiny white umbels in arid semi-desert climate
harvestingIndicator: Umbels turn greyish-brown; harvest early morning to prevent shattering.
introTipEn: Shallow sowing (1–1.5 cm) is critical for germination; spray Mancozeb proactively whenever overcast cloudy skies develop to prevent devastating blight.
efficiencyGain: 30% protection against blight with timely preventative sprays
micronutrientNote: Apply Sulphur 10 kg/acre and multi-micronutrient spray at flowering to enhance essential oil aroma.
stagnationAlert: Cumin roots rot in wet soils; irrigate with very light flow in micro-sprinklers.

fertilizerStages.applicationMethod: Mix well in soil during final land preparation
Broadcast post weeding with light irrigation
Foliar mist spray at early seed development

irrigation.frequencyEn: Very light irrigations; only 3–4 during crop cycle
irrigation.criticalStagesEn: Germination (first light watering), Branching (30 DAS), and Seed Filling (65 DAS)
irrigation.tipsEn: Never irrigate during cloudy, humid, or stormy weather as it triggers blight outbreak.

pestsDiseases.symptomsEn: Minute dark brown spots on leaves and stems; plants turn blackish and droop rapidly in cloudy weather.
pestsDiseases.controlEn: Preventative spray with Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L); on symptom onset spray Propiconazole 25 EC (1 ml/L).

pestsDiseases.symptomsEn: White powdery patches cover stems and umbels, shriveling seeds.
pestsDiseases.controlEn: Dust wettable Sulphur 80 WP (2.5 g/L) or Dinocap (1 ml/L).

pestsDiseases.symptomsEn: Tiny yellow-green aphids suck sap from umbels and flowers during cool mornings.
pestsDiseases.controlEn: Spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG (0.4 g/L) or Dimethoate 30 EC (1.5 ml/L).

harvestSteps.textEn: Umbels turn greyish-brown and seeds harden to touch.
Harvest early morning while dew is present to minimize seed shattering.
Dry plants on clean plastic tarpaulins in sun for 3–4 days.
Beat gently with light sticks; clean with fine sieves. Expected yield: 4–7 Qtl/acre.
